frequencyResponse.interpretation: A maximum among four coarse prescribed frequencies is not an Arnold-tongue boundary or a free-response lock-in point.

weakAmplitudeAuditAt056Hz.interpretation: This checks local amplitude consistency at one unresolved grid; it is not a continuum-limit linear-response proof.

gridPhaseSeedAuditAt056Hz.interpretation: The seed changes only the declared sub-cell grid phase in this deterministic backend; one pair is a sensitivity diagnostic, not a stochastic uncertainty estimate.

allowedConclusions: The native 2-D backend can measure a complex prescribed-motion line-force response and its mean power without a 3-D strip closure.
Force amplitude alone is insufficient: the sign of mean work is controlled by force-velocity phase and non-first-harmonic remainder.
Residual and dual-force-path diagnostics quantify whether a one-harmonic structural reduction is currently trustworthy.
prohibitedConclusions: Do not infer a three-dimensional total pendulum torque or apparatus amplitude from these line loads.
Do not call the largest sampled response a lock-in boundary, and do not calibrate ROM coefficients before grid/Mach/domain/penalty/time convergence.
Do not relabel this study as validated 2-D reference evidence; the phase-3 grid verdict remains INCONCLUSIVE.

allowedConclusions: The same frozen equations can remain observably dependent on initial wake amplitude for hundreds of seconds near a weak spectral crossing.
A finite-duration visibility threshold can differ materially from the zero-state spectral threshold even without true multistability.
Cold/hot comparisons are a necessary diagnostic before interpreting an up/down sweep as a branch fold.
prohibitedConclusions: Do not interpret a cold/hot difference before the stationarity gates as hysteresis or multiple attractors.
Do not quote these speeds as apparatus thresholds because the coefficient package is an illustrative literature prior.
Do not promote frequency proximity to L1 without bounded phase, power, periodic-orbit, and Floquet evidence.

isolatedWakeFiniteTimeVisibilityBoundary.exactRadialSolution: r(t)^{-2}=beta/mu+[r(0)^{-2}-beta/mu] exp(-2 mu t), with the continuous mu->0 limit
isolatedWakeFiniteTimeVisibilityBoundary.limitOrder: At fixed nonzero detection amplitude, T->infinity solves mu=beta*r_det^2 rather than mu=0. The spectral boundary is recovered only with the additional r_det->0 limit.
isolatedWakeFiniteTimeVisibilityBoundary.interpretation: This is the isolated frozen-prior wake visibility boundary V_obs(T), not the coupled mechanical visibility boundary and not an apparatus prediction.

reasons: Strouhal and lift RMS are not in a monotone asymptotic three-grid sequence.
The last 10 s contain only three to four complete lift periods per grid.
The penalty-reaction/stress-contour force discrepancy remains 15% or larger on the fine grid.

boundariesUnderIllustrativePrior.epistemicStatus: mathematical output of an uncalibrated literature-prior coefficient package; not an apparatus threshold prediction

nominalPriorPoint.observation: the default 12 s run is shorter than the isolated-wake logarithmic saturation-time estimate

extendedPriorRun.interpretation: Numerical completion alone does not certify a stationary periodic orbit; block stationarity and Floquet analysis remain separate gates.

crossBackendFrequencyDiscriminator.interpretation: The CFD range is a nonconverged discriminator, not a calibrated replacement coefficient. Its mismatch with the ROM prior quantifies a model-form uncertainty that must be resolved by accepted CFD or fixed-body experiment.

allowedConclusions: The frozen equations admit distinct fixed-wake, coupled-equilibrium, synchronization, and visibility boundaries.
For the bundled prior, 12 s numerical completion is not evidence of a stationary nonlinear branch.
The independent 2-D CFD study supplies a useful but unresolved Strouhal discriminator.
prohibitedConclusions: Do not quote either computed speed as an experimental critical velocity.
Do not call the extended prior trajectory a validated branch or the CFD Strouhal range converged.
Do not infer three-dimensional apparatus loads from the two-dimensional grid study.

synthesisRules: Only compare native dimensionless frequency, phase, line-force gain, and line-power sign across the two-dimensional and reduced-order layers.
Never compare the phase-3 line force per unit span directly with the phase-1 finite-span generalized torque.
Treat disagreement as a model-form discriminator until both coefficient calibration and high-fidelity convergence gates pass.
Retain U/UNKNOWN whenever finite-time, stationarity, periodic-orbit, or load-convergence gates are missing.
